CVE-2026-34591.description: Poetry is a dependency manager for Python. From version 1.4.0 to before version 2.3.3, a crafted wheel can contain ../ paths that Poetry writes to disk without containment checks, allowing arbitrary file write with the privileges of the Poetry process. It is reachable from untrusted package artifacts during normal install flows. (Normally, installing a malicious wheel is not sufficient for execution of malicious code. Malicious code will only be executed after installation if the malicious package is imported or invoked by the user.). This issue has been patched in version 2.3.3.

CVE-2026-41140.description: Poetry is a dependency manager for Python. Prior to 2.3.4, the extractall() function in src/poetry/utils/helpers.py:410-426 extracts sdist tarballs without path traversal protection on Python versions where tarfile.data_filter is unavailable. Considering only Python versions which are still supported by Poetry, these are 3.10.0 - 3.10.12 and 3.11.0 - 3.11.4. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.3.4.

GHSA-cm45-jwqh-659g.title: Tar extraction fix bypass via symlink and parent traversal on fallback Python 3.10.0 - 3.10.12 and 3.11.0 - 3.11.4
GHSA-cm45-jwqh-659g.description: ### Summary Poetry 2.4.1 still contains a bypass of the GHSA-73h3-mf4w-8647 tar extraction fix on Python versions that use Poetry's fallback extractor branch, currently Python 3.10.0 - 3.10.12 and 3.11.0 - 3.11.4. The fallback validates tar member paths and symlink targets with `os.path.abspath()` before calling `tarfile.extractall()`, but it does not model symlink traversal for later regular file members. A tar member sequence containing a symlink `a -> .` followed by a regular file named `a/../outside/pwn.txt` passes the lexical `is_relative_to(dest)` check because `abspath(dest / 'a/../outside/pwn.txt')` is `dest/outside/pwn.txt`. During extraction, however, the filesystem resolves `a` as a symlink to `dest`; the following `..` component then escapes to the parent of `dest`, so the file is written outside the extraction directory. ### Impact Arbitrary file write (path traversal) from untrusted sdist content. **In practice, the impact is low** because an attacker who exploits this vulnerability can as well include arbitrary code in a setup.py, which will be executed when the sdist is built after tar extraction. In other words, a malicious sdist can write arbitrary files by design. However, since it is unexpected and not by design that the file write already happens during tar extraction, this is still considered a vulnerability. ### Patches Versions 2.4.2 and newer of Poetry ensure that paths are inside the target directory. ### Technical details The vulnerable fallback is in `src/poetry/utils/helpers.py`: ```python dest = Path(os.path.abspath(dest)) safe_members = [] for member in archive.getmembers(): member_path = Path(os.path.abspath(dest / member.name)) if not member_path.is_relative_to(dest): raise ValueError(...) if member.issym(): link_target = Path(os.path.abspath(member_path.parent / member.linkname)) if not link_target.is_relative_to(dest): raise ValueError(...) elif member.islnk(): link_target = Path(os.path.abspath(dest / member.linkname)) if not link_target.is_relative_to(dest): raise ValueError(...) safe_members.append(member) archive.extractall(dest, members=safe_members) ``` Direct `../` paths, absolute paths, direct symlinks outside `dest`, and direct hardlinks outside `dest` are rejected. The bypass uses a symlink that is itself inside the destination (`a -> .`) and a later regular file whose archive name is lexically normalized before symlink resolution. ### Reproduction ```python import io import tarfile import tempfile from pathlib import Path from poetry.utils import helpers base = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='poetry-tar-bypass-')) dest = base / 'dest' outside = base / 'outside' dest.mkdir() outside.mkdir() tar_path = base / 'poc.tar' with tarfile.open(tar_path, 'w') as tf: symlink = tarfile.TarInfo('a') symlink.type = tarfile.SYMTYPE symlink.linkname = '.' tf.addfile(symlink) data = b'owned\n' regular = tarfile.TarInfo('a/../outside/pwn.txt') regular.size = len(data) tf.addfile(regular, io.BytesIO(data)) # Only needed on newer Python to demonstrate the fallback branch locally. # On Python 3.10.12 or 3.11.4, Poetry enters this branch itself. old_version_info = helpers.sys.version_info helpers.sys.version_info = (3, 10, 12) try: helpers.extractall(tar_path, dest, zip=False) finally: helpers.sys.version_info = old_version_info print((outside / 'pwn.txt').exists(), outside / 'pwn.txt') ``` Expected output: ```text True /tmp/poetry-tar-bypass-.../outside/pwn.txt ``` ### Remediation Use `tarfile.extractall(..., filter='data')` wherever available. For fallback Python versions, avoid a pre-validation pass that only uses lexical paths. Either reject links entirely in fallback mode or implement extraction with per-member resolved path checks against the live filesystem state before opening each output file. For regular file members, resolve the final path after accounting for symlinks in already-extracted ancestors, and reject if the resolved target is outside `dest`.

GHSA-xvhx-496r-7682.title: Lockfile hash pinning fails open when a source index serves a candidate with no hash and a filename the lock does not list
GHSA-xvhx-496r-7682.description: ## Summary **Poetry is supposed to bind every installed artifact to the sha256 (or other hash) recorded under files in poetry.lock.** Two layers do that binding, and both can be skipped by data the index controls, so a lock that pins a hash can still install an artifact nobody hashed. 1. The chooser accepts any candidate link that advertises no hash at all, without ever comparing anything to the locked hashes. 2. The executor's post-download hash check only runs when the downloaded archive's filename appears in the lock's files list. Serve the artifact under a filename the lock does not list and that check never runs. Put those together and a source index that omits the hash fragment and offers a plausible unlisted filename installs a fully unverified artifact, even though the lock pins a sha256 for that package. ## Impact A lockfile that pins sha256 for a package provides no integrity guarantee for a link that the index serves without a hash under an unlisted filename. The affected artifact installs unverified, which is exactly the property the lock is meant to provide. This does not hit PyPI, whose simple index always emits #sha256= fragments. The realistic setting is a self-hosted or corporate PEP 503 index configured as a Poetry source (devpi, Nexus, Artifactory, a plain directory served over HTTP, an internal mirror), many of which omit the hash fragment. A compromised or malicious index of that shape, or an on-path attacker against a plain-HTTP index, serves the target package under a filename the lock does not list (a build-tag variant, a different wheel tag, .zip instead of .tar.gz) with no hash fragment, and Poetry installs it. The lockfile author believes hashes are pinned. For that link they are not enforced. Since a wheel or sdist runs project-controlled code at import (and an sdist at build), a swapped artifact is code execution in the victim's environment. ## Where it is src/poetry/installation/chooser.py, _get_links (lines 210-240 at HEAD). After computing locked_hashes from package.files, the per-link loop opens with: ``` for link in links: if not link.hashes: selected_links.append(link) continue ``` A link that carries no hash fragment is appended to selected_links unconditionally. The link_hash not in locked_hashes rejection two lines further down (line 231) is never reached for that link, and the repository.calculate_sha256(link) fallback at line 228-229 is only taken for links that already advertise a hash of a different type. So 'no hash offered' is treated as 'accept', not 'go compute and compare'. src/poetry/installation/executor.py, _populate_hashes_dict (lines 789-792 at HEAD): ``` def _populate_hashes_dict(self, archive: Path, package: Package) -> None: if package.files and archive.name in {f['file'] for f in package.files}: archive_hash = self._validate_archive_hash(archive, package) self._hashes[package.name] = archive_hash ``` _validate_archive_hash (lines 794-814) is the real check, and it does raise on mismatch. But it only runs when archive.name is in the lock's file set. If the served filename is not one the lock lists, the whole if is false, nothing is validated, and self._hashes[package.name] is never even populated, so the recorded install metadata carries no hash either.. ## Proof of concept I built two wheels for one package, demo-pkg 1.0.0: a benign one and an attacker one with different bytes. I stood up two local PEP 503 indexes and pointed a Poetry project at the source. Step 1, lock against an honest index. The index page linked the benign wheel with a #sha256= fragment: ```html demo_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl ``` poetry lock recorded, in poetry.lock: ```toml files = [ {file = 'demo_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl', hash = 'sha256:81b12ea2...512a'}, ] ``` Step 2, swap the source to serve the attacker artifact. Same source URL, now serving a build-tag variant filename the lock does not list, and with no hash fragment (this models a compromised or MITM'd index; pyproject.toml and poetry.lock are untouched, so the lock still pins sha256:81b1...512a): ```html demo_pkg-1.0.0-1-py3-none-any.whl ``` The attacker wheel's real sha256 is fd58a1f0...d36a, which is not the pinned hash. Step 3, poetry install. It installed: ``` Package operations: 1 install, 0 updates, 0 removals - Installing demo-pkg (1.0.0) - ``` and the installed demo_pkg/__init__.py was the attacker copy: ```python MALICIOUS = 'ATTACKER CONTROLLED PAYLOAD - lockfile pinned a sha256 but this unhashed artifact was installed' ``` So the pinned-sha256 lock installed an artifact with a different, unverified hash. Control, to isolate that the filename is the bypass. I re-served the same attacker bytes but under the listed filename demo_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl (still no hash fragment). This time _populate_hashes_dict's filename check matched, _validate_archive_hash ran, and Poetry failed closed: ``` RuntimeError Hash for demo-pkg (1.0.0) from archive demo_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl not found in known hashes (was: sha256:fd58a1f0...d36a) at .../poetry/installation/executor.py:795 in _validate_archive_hash ``` The only difference between the install that went through and the one that was caught is the served filename: an unlisted filename skips the check entirely, a listed filename gets caught. That pins the bug to the two lines above (chooser accepting the no-hash link, executor gating validation on filename membership). ## Suggested fix Two small changes, either of which closes it, both is better: - chooser.py _get_links: when locked_hashes is non-empty and link.hashes is empty, do not accept the link. Fall through to the repository.calculate_sha256(link) branch that already exists a few lines down (line 228-229) so the downloaded bytes are hashed and compared, or skip the link. Concretely, guard the early accept the way uv does: only treat 'no hash on the link' as acceptable when no hash was locked for this package. - executor.py _populate_hashes_dict: when package.files is non-empty but archive.name matches none of the listed files, raise instead of silently returning. A downloaded artifact whose filename is not in the lock is not something to install quietly.
